questionsToConsider: What standards were shoppers briefed on, and does each one have a matching question?
Which store areas belong in the condition grid for your type of business?
Do you want receipts as proof of visit, and how will you handle any personal details on them?
Should shoppers name staff, or describe them, given your policies?
guide.howToUseResponses: Compare reports across branches and visit times rather than reacting to a single visit, since one bad afternoon is not a pattern. Look at greeting times, stock availability and what staff did when an item was missing, which are the most coachable moments. Share specific, factual observations with store managers, and use the overall score against the brief to track each location over time.
customizeSteps: Edit the questions so they match your brief exactly, and replace the store-condition rows with your own checklist.
Add the store or branch as a URL parameter in each shopper's link so it arrives prefilled.
Send each shopper their link before the visit, then export reports to CSV to compare branches side by side.

faqs.q: What should a mystery shopper survey include?
faqs.a: Visit details, how quickly the shopper was greeted, store condition, staff knowledge, product availability, the checkout and a factual written account, with space for receipts or photos.

faqs.q: How do I keep mystery shopper reports objective?
faqs.a: Ask what happened, not how it felt: times, actions and what staff said. Rating questions work best when the scale is tied to the standard the shopper was briefed on.

faqs.q: Can mystery shoppers upload receipts and photos?
faqs.a: Yes. This template includes an upload question that accepts images and PDFs, so shoppers can attach proof of visit and any photos they are allowed to take.

faqs.q: Does it work for phone or online mystery shopping?
faqs.a: Yes. Choosing a phone or online visit skips the question about the store's condition, and the rest of the report still applies.
